title: Leader Visibility Is Even More Important When Team Members Work Remotely
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article makes the case that visibility, showing up physically and consistently, is a defining trait of trusted leaders, and that it becomes even more critical for remote teams. It contrasts leaders who hide behind busy schedules and merely announce their availability with leaders who actively seek out interaction across different settings and mediums. The piece argues that visible leaders build trust, model desired behaviors in real time, and create the transparency remote teams especially need to stay aligned with shared goals and vision. It closes by extending the same principle to how leaders should engage clients and industry peers.
points: Visibility, not just accessibility, is what builds trust and connection with a team.
Leaders who merely announce their availability are rarely approached and become isolated.
Visible leaders model desired behaviors in real time across different settings.
Remote teams need visibility even more, since it substitutes for face-to-face alignment on goals and vision.
The same visibility principle extends to how leaders engage clients, customers, and industry peers.
quotes: Good leaders are everywhere. They know that the team wants to see them, hear from them, and question them.
Sequestered leaders often attempt to make up for their seclusion by announcing their accessibility if and when others need them.
Visible leaders also have the advantage of leading by example.
For teams that work and engage remotely, a leader’s visibility is even more important.
They commit to seeing important stakeholders face-to-face and often speak at events and attend conferences to support the team.
In a world where attention is a critical currency, the best leaders work hard to be as visible as they can.
